claims.text: Catalytic activity in nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs solid-solution catalysts is governed by surface composition.
Catalytic activity in nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs solid-solution catalysts is governed by surface electronic structure.
Catalytic activity can be optimized by controlled manipulation of alloy composition and structure.
The initial nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst has uniform composition.
The initial nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst has a uniform structure.
XPS or STM can be used in situ to characterize and manipulate the catalyst's surface composition and electronic structure.
Surface composition influences adsorption and desorption of reactants and products.
Surface electronic structure influences adsorption and desorption of reactants and products.
Changes in reactant and product adsorption and desorption affect catalytic activity.
Optimizing surface composition and electronic structure will increase catalytic activity relative to the unmodified catalyst.
The increased catalytic activity will be observable as an enhanced ethanol oxidation rate.
The proposed relationship is expected to hold at 250–350 °C, 1–5 atm, and reactant concentrations of 1–10%.
Temperatures of 250–350 °C, pressures of 1–5 atm, and reactant concentrations of 1–10% are typical ethanol oxidation conditions.
The exact relationship among surface composition, electronic structure, and catalytic activity is uncertain.
